findings.quote: 1.1.9 "Proprietary Materials" means any and all proprietary, technical, scientific, operational, organizational, commercial, financial, or business information, data, software, methodologies, architectures, algorithms, protocols, schemas, specifications, business plans, customer data, and documentation disclosed or made accessible by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party to the Receiving Party or its Representatives, whether orally, visually, electronically, digitally, or in tangible documentary form, before, on, or after the Effective Date, that is marked or identified as confidential or proprietary, or that reasonably ought to be understood as confidential given the nature of the information or the circumstances attending its disclosure.
findings.why: Jev reads the clause as matches preferred against PB02 Definition of Confidential Information (pass 0.75, breach 0.23, unclear 0.02).

findings.quote: 2.1 The Receiving Party shall treat and preserve as strictly confidential all Proprietary Materials of the Disclosing Party and shall not, without the prior written authorization of the Disclosing Party, disclose, disseminate, publish, or make available such Proprietary Materials, directly or indirectly, in whole or in part, to any Person other than its Representatives who strictly need to know such information for the implementation and progression of the Authorized Purpose.
findings.draft_redline: "Representatives" means, with respect to a Party, that Party's and its Affiliates' respective directors, officers, employees, independent contractors, professional advisers, accountants, auditors and insurers.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like insurers to be included among permitted recipients; the rest of the Representatives definition works for us.
findings.why: Jev reads the clause as unclear against PB05 Permitted disclosure to Representatives and Group (pass 0.25, breach 0.31, unclear 0.44).

findings.quote: 2.2 The Receiving Party shall exercise the same degree of care to avoid unauthorized disclosure, dissemination, or utilization of the Proprietary Materials as it employs with respect to its own confidential materials of a similar high sensitivity, but under no circumstances less than a reasonable standard of professional care.
findings.why: Substantive term that no playbook rule covers (Jev other_term 0.99).

findings.quote: 2.3 The Receiving Party shall not use, exploit, reproduce, adapt, or process the Proprietary Materials of the Disclosing Party for any purpose, commercial or non-commercial, other than strictly in furtherance of the Authorized Purpose.
findings.why: Jev reads the clause as unclear against PB03 Purpose limitation (pass 0.48, breach 0.13, unclear 0.39).

The Receiving Party shall remain fully responsible and liable for any breach of the terms of this Agreement caused by the act, error, or omission of any of its Representatives.
findings.why: Jev reads the clause as matches preferred against PB05 Permitted disclosure to Representatives and Group (pass 0.64, breach 0.06, unclear 0.30).

findings.quote: 2.5 The Receiving Party shall refrain from disassembling, decompiling, reverse engineering, decrypting, or otherwise attempting to discover or reconstruct the composition, logic, underlying concepts, or source code of any software, models, frameworks, algorithms, or prototypes furnished by the Disclosing Party that embody Proprietary Materials.

Jev reads the clause as matches preferred against PB04 Carve-outs (pass 1.00, breach 0.00, unclear 0.00).

findings.quote:
4.1 If the Receiving Party or any of its Representatives is legally ordered, compelled, or requested pursuant to Applicable Law, valid judicial order, or the lawful order of a competent governmental, administrative, or supervisory agency to disclose any Proprietary Materials, the Receiving Party shall:
4.1.1 immediately notify the Disclosing Party in writing of such legal requirement, to the extent legally permissible, so that the Disclosing Party may seek an appropriate protective order or other legal remedy;
4.1.2 provide reasonable cooperation and assistance to the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party's sole expense, in seeking such protective measures or limiting the scope of disclosure; and
4.1.3 disclose, if such disclosure is ultimately required, only that precise portion of the Proprietary Materials that is legally required to be disclosed based on the written advice of its qualified legal counsel.
findings.why: Jev reads the clause as matches preferred against PB06 Compelled disclosure (pass 1.00, breach 0.00, unclear 0.00).

findings.quote: 5.3 To the extent that the Receiving Party, in the course of evaluating the Proprietary Materials or participating in discussions concerning the Authorized Purpose, generates, suggests, develops, or contributes any modifications, adaptations, improvements, derivative works, or feedback relating to the Disclosing Party's software, technology, or Proprietary Materials, all Intellectual Property Rights in such modifications, adaptations, improvements, derivative works, and feedback shall vest exclusively in Vanderberg upon creation, and Halyard hereby assigns to Vanderberg, with full title guarantee, all such Intellectual Property Rights free from encumbrances.
findings.draft_redline: Delete clause 5.3. Each Party retains ownership of its own Intellectual Property Rights, including in any modifications, improvements or feedback relating to its own software, technology or Proprietary Materials, and no licence is granted other than for the Authorized Purpose.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We cannot agree to assign IP in feedback or improvements to one Party only. We propose deleting clause 5.3 so that each Party keeps its own IP.
findings.why: Jev reads the clause as breaches against PB08 Ownership, licences and IP (pass 0.00, breach 1.00, unclear 0.00).

findings.quote: 6.1 Upon the written demand of the Disclosing Party, or upon the termination or expiry of this Agreement, the Receiving Party shall immediately cease all use of the Disclosing Party's Proprietary Materials.

findings.quote: 6.2 Within forty-eight (48) hours of receipt of a written notice from the Disclosing Party requesting the return or destruction of Proprietary Materials, the Receiving Party shall deliver to the Disclosing Party, or permanently destroy, delete, and expunge from all computers, servers, storage media, and electronic repositories, all documents, tangible records, electronic files, copies, reproductions, extracts, and summaries containing or reflecting any Proprietary Materials, without exception, and an authorized officer of the Receiving Party shall promptly confirm compliance in writing to the Disclosing Party.
findings.draft_redline: Within ten (10) Business Days of receipt of a written notice from the Disclosing Party requesting the return or destruction of Proprietary Materials, the Receiving Party shall return or destroy them.
findings.note_to_counterparty: A 48-hour deadline is not practicable for us; we propose ten Business Days for return or destruction.
findings.why: Jev reads the clause as breaches against PB07 Return and destruction (pass 0.00, breach 1.00, unclear 0.00).
